title: Cross-region audit replication truncation during downstream cert rotation - follow-up
creator: Sara Liu
description: Summary: During a routine certificate rotation in europe-west the audit-replication service observed a transient schema mismatch which caused replication workers to truncate the last 18 hours of audit events for the eu region before requeueing. This produced an apparent gap in the centralized audit store and caused alerts from SOC and Compliance. No private keys were exposed; the primary impact is gaps in audit retention and incomplete entries for cross-region authorization events. This ticket tracks remediation actions, long-term mitigations, and compliance reporting deliverables.
investigation: 2026-02-25: On-call alerted by Compliance after missing entries surfaced in the centralized audit dashboard for europe-west. Initial triage found replication worker restarts coincident with cert rotation window.

2026-02-25: Team recreated the failure in staging by rotating certs while a high-throughput audit writer was active; observed that consumer library rejected events with a new envelope header version and the replication worker applied a fallback that truncated pending batches.

2026-02-26: Root cause: a backward-incompatible change to the audit transport envelope (header v2) was deployed to the europe-west forwarding agent one hour before cert rotation. When the agent restarted with new certs, the replication worker reprocessed a mixed queue containing v1 and v2 envelopes; a defensive deserialization path treated unknown fields as a fatal error and marked the batch as corrupted, causing a truncate-and-skip behavior. This behavior predated our stricter CI checks because the change was gated only by unit tests not an integration contract test.

2026-02-27: Impact quantification: ~72k audit events from 2026-02-24 18:00 to 2026-02-25 12:30 (eu-west) were missing from the central store. Cross-region queries surfaced the gap, SLO for audit retention missed for 14 hours. No customer data exfiltration detected. Compliance notified and internal incident report filed.

2026-03-02: Temporary recovery: we recovered ~58k events by replaying archived transport logs and re-ingesting transformed events after writing a tolerant parser. Remaining ~14k events lacked complete headers and were annotated as partial entries in the archive.

2026-03-05: Postmortem review with Security and Compliance. Agreed follow-up scope: prevent envelope breaking changes, harden replication worker error handling, add contract/integration tests, and provide evidence package for auditors.
action_items: OWNER: Diego Ramos — Implement tolerant parser with schema fallback in replication worker; return to strict mode only after cross-region contract verification. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-18

OWNER: Priya Nair — Add integration-level contract test in CI that simulates cert rotation + mixed-envelope traffic; block merges that introduce envelope header changes without a compatibility migration plan. Estimate: 2. Due: 2026-03-12
OWNER: Security Team (lead: Marco Alvarez) — Prepare compliance evidence package (timeline, recovered objects list, hash digests, mitigation plan) for external auditors. Due: 2026-03-22

OWNER: Reliability (lead: Hannah Park) — Add replication worker alert that detects >5% batch-corruption rate and auto-switches to read-only recovery mode plus paged re-ingest. Estimate: 3. Due: 2026-03-20

OWNER: DevEx (lead: Owen Chen) — Publish a runbook for cert rotations that includes pre-checks for backward-compatible transport changes and a checklist for rolling forward tolerant parsers before agent restarts. Due: 2026-03-14
